narrative:
On September 9, 2026, the Karnataka High Court listed 3,043 matters across 45 judges and took up 1,346 for hearing, translating to an overall hearing rate of 44.2%. This marks a decline compared to the preceding sessions, down from 51.4% (1,386 heard of 2,696 scheduled) on September 8 and 48.5% on September 7, though remaining considerably higher than the 35.6% clearance seen on September 3.

Bench productivity showed notable variation depending on list composition. Justice C.M. Poonacha recorded the highest volume of hearings, taking up 116 of 156 listed matters (74.4%). High conversion was also achieved by Justice E.S. Indiresh, who heard 65 of 78 matters (83.3%), and Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar, who took up 53 of 65 cases (81.5%). In contrast, heavily burdened boards saw limited progress; in Hall 7, Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad took up only 1 of 279 matters on a supplementary list, alongside 10 of 140 cases heard on a separate cause list.

Stage-wise analysis reveals steady handling of procedural matters but continued compression in substantive arguments. The Orders stage achieved the highest conversion among major stages at 58.1% (385 of 663 heard), improving slightly from 55.7% on September 8. Admission stages converted 51.2% (432 of 843), while Final Hearing proceedings remained subdued at 29.2% (172 of 590 heard), consistent with the 28.8% logged the previous day. Further Hearing matters saw the sharpest drop, converting only 4.6% (15 of 323).

By case type, Writ Petitions constituted the largest volume at 1,420 cases, but their hearing rate slipped to 38.5% (546 heard) from 52.9% on September 8. Criminal Petitions sustained stable clearance at 54.4% (258 of 474 heard), while Regular Second Appeals demonstrated strong conversion, with 58.1% of listed matters (104 of 179) heard.
